description: Portable conformance fixtures for the Axiom Server IR. Each entry is a self-contained JSON document: the Server IR, the state to start from, the principals, the invocations to perform and the results required. Running them needs no part of this implementation. "conformance" above is the fixture-FORMAT version (axiom.conformance.v1/v2); each fixture entry's own "contract" is the Server IR contract THAT fixture requires — the two are independent axes and neither implies the other.

fixtures.name: mutation-commits
fixtures.description: An action within its guards commits every write, and derived state follows.

fixtures.name: guard-refuses
fixtures.description: A guard that does not hold refuses the invocation, naming its failure mode.

fixtures.name: constraint-rolls-back
fixtures.description: Iteration N sees the writes of iterations before it, so two lines for one part are counted together — and the invariant then rolls the whole action back.

fixtures.name: for-each-provisional
fixtures.description: The same two-line shape, within stock: 10 − 4 − 4, not 10 − 4 twice.

fixtures.name: transition-constraint
fixtures.description: A rule about how state may change refuses a raise, and permits a fall.

fixtures.name: authorization
fixtures.description: Authorization is evaluated on the authority, with the caller bound to PRINCIPAL.

fixtures.name: argument-validation
fixtures.description: Untrusted arguments are checked against declared parameter types.

fixtures.name: idempotent-retry
fixtures.description: A repeated request id is answered from the record, not executed again.

fixtures.name: concurrent-invocations
fixtures.description: Three callers each want four of a stock of five. Exactly one may commit; the rest are refused by the guard against authoritative state.

fixtures.name: restart
fixtures.description: Committed state is restored exactly on restart, and a rolled-back write never reappears.

fixtures.name: integration-query-success
fixtures.description: A successful integration query binds its result and commits.

fixtures.name: integration-query-timeout
fixtures.description: A non-cooperating adapter cannot wedge the invocation past its declared timeoutMs; the runtime enforces the deadline itself.

fixtures.name: timed-trigger-polling
fixtures.description: An interval trigger fires the query and writes its result, with no real wait.

fixtures.name: effect-success-event
fixtures.description: A succeeded effect dispatches its structured outcome to a system-only follow-up action — never reachable by a client directly.

fixtures.name: system-only-action-rejects-client
fixtures.description: An anonymous client cannot directly invoke an action reachable only by a trigger, event or effect outcome.

fixtures.name: late-query-result-after-timeout
fixtures.description: A query that eventually resolves successfully, but only after its declared timeoutMs already answered, is discarded — the late success can never mutate state.

fixtures.name: late-query-rejection-after-timeout
fixtures.description: A query that eventually rejects, but only after its declared timeoutMs already answered, is discarded exactly like a late success — the invocation already failed with INTEGRATION_TIMEOUT, not the provider error.

fixtures.name: failed-effect-structured-outcome
fixtures.description: A failed effect dispatches its structured failure outcome (code, message, retryable) to a system-only follow-up action — no text parsing required.

fixtures.name: authenticated-client-rejects-system-only-action
fixtures.description: An authenticated client is refused by a system-only action exactly like an anonymous one — invocation.allowedSources checks the request's source, not the caller's identity.

fixtures.name: simultaneous-same-instant-triggers-both-commit
fixtures.description: Two one-shot delay triggers due at the same simulated instant are serialized against each other, not raced — both commit, with no spurious conflict.

fixtures.name: rolled-back-action-produces-no-effect
fixtures.description: A constraint violation rolls back the whole transaction, including the effect intent it recorded within it — no adapter call, no outcome event.

fixtures.name: effect-retry-sequence
fixtures.description: A transient failure (retryable: true) is retried under the declared fixed-delay policy and eventually dispatches a success outcome.

fixtures.name: event-payload-invalid
fixtures.description: A malformed event payload is rejected before any bound action sees it.

fixtures.name: verified-external-event-invokes-system-only-action
fixtures.description: A verified external event — semantically, an ordinary event dispatch, since HTTP delivery and signature verification are host/adapter concerns outside the graph — invokes a system-only action through its bound trigger, never reachable by a direct client InvokeRequest.
